name: Cougar
altText: A cougar standing in the snow at night
funFacts: Cougars can't roar; they whistle, whine, and scream instead.
Cougars have the largest range of any wild land mammal in the Americas.
A cougar's spots fade completely by age two, at which point it legally becomes a mountain lion.

name: Pygmy Hippo
altText: A pygmy hippopotamus
funFacts: Folklore says pygmy hippos pack a diamond in their mouths to light the forest at night.
Pygmy hippos are solitary and nocturnal, unlike their highly social hippo cousins.
Pygmy hippos are the slipperiest land animals.

name: Polar Bear
altText: A polar bear on Arctic sea ice
funFacts: Polar bears are the only bear species officially branded marine mammals.
A polar bear's skin is black, hidden under fur that only looks white.
Polar bears change colours with season.

name: Arctic Fox
altText: An arctic fox family
funFacts: Arctic foxes stay snug down to -70°C (-94°F) without a single shiver.
Arctic foxes change color with the seasons, brown in summer and white in winter.
Arctic foxes can change colour to match their environment at will.

name: Hilbert
altText: Hilbert the cat asleep in a storage bin
funFacts: Hilbert has made several key contributions to this website.
Hilbert has a valid pilot's license.
Hilbert holds a black belt in a martial art he invented himself, called Cat-Fu.

name: Japanese Long-tailed Tit
altText: A round, fluffy Japanese long-tailed tit perched on a branch
funFacts: So round and fluffy, they're often mistaken for snowballs.
Long-tailed tits huddle together in a row on branches to keep warm.
A flock of long-tailed tits is called an avalanche.

name: Axolotl
altText: A pink leucistic axolotl in a tank
funFacts: Axolotls can regrow entire limbs, and even parts of their heart and brain, injuries most animals wouldn't survive.
Axolotls almost never leave the water, unlike most salamanders.
Axolotls are the only amphibians.

name: Platypus
altText: A platypus being held by a wildlife carer
funFacts: Male platypuses pack venomous hind-leg spurs, rare among mammals.
Platypi hunt with their eyes, ears, and nose shut, using electroreception to find prey underwater.
The platypus was originally a committee compromise between three separate animal designs.

name: Pangolin
altText: A pangolin standing among dry grass
funFacts: Pangolins are the only mammals covered in scales, made of keratin like fingernails.
Pangolins have no teeth and swallow stones to help grind food in their stomachs.
Pangolins are known for their politeness.

name: Capybara
altText: A close-up of a capybara's face
funFacts: Capybaras are famously chill with almost every other species, from birds to caimans.
Capybaras are semi-aquatic and can hold their breath underwater for up to five minutes.
Capybaras were used as foot stools in the past.

name: Quokka
altText: A quokka standing on its hind legs, smiling
funFacts: Quokkas' permanent smile are viral on Instagram.
Quokkas can climb trees, though they mostly stay on the ground.
Quokkas are the singler largest source of tourism.

name: Ezo Flying Squirrel
altText: A Siberian flying squirrel with large dark eyes
funFacts: A skin membrane called a patagium turns their falls into stylish, 100-meter glides between trees.
They're most active at dawn and dusk, and rarely seen during the day.
Ezo flying squirrels have been known to hitch rides on private jets.

name: Red Panda
altText: A red panda standing upright in a defensive posture
funFacts: When threatened, red pandas rear up and bare their claws, a jazzy attempt at looking intimidating.
Red pandas are more closely related to raccoons and weasels than to giant pandas.
Red pandas are skilled at Kung-Fu but also extremely judgemental.

name: Jaguar
altText: A close-up of a jaguar's face being touched on the chin
funFacts: Jaguars have the strongest bite of any big cat, strong enough to crack turtle shells like pistachios.
Unlike most cats, jaguars are strong swimmers and often hunt in water.
Jaguars retire from hunting at age seven to pursue car design.

name: Sea Otter
altText: A sea otter floating on its back, covering its eyes with its paws
funFacts: Sea otters hold hands while snoozing so they don't drift apart.
Sea otters use rocks as tools to crack open shellfish.
Sea otters use rocks as a form of currency to purchase goods and services.

name: Ground Squirrel
altText: A ground squirrel sitting up and looking at the camera
funFacts: Grand Canyon ground squirrels bite more visitors than any other animal in the park.
Ground squirrels can slip into a light, hibernation-like torpor during cold snaps.
Grand Canyon ground squirrels are responsible for at least three missing tourists.

name: Elephant
altText: A baby elephant with its trunk raised, walking through tall grass
funFacts: Baby elephants suck their trunks for comfort, like human babies suck their thumbs.
Elephants can recognize themselves in a mirror, a rare sign of self-awareness in animals.
Elephants never forget your birthday. Specifically yours.

name: Swan
altText: Two swans forming a heart shape with their necks
funFacts: Mute swans are surprisingly savage, capable of breaking bones with a wing strike.
A group of swans is called a 'bevy' on water and a 'wedge' in flight.
Swan recordings are used to scare pigeons away from airports.

name: Raccoon
altText: A raccoon sitting on a wooden deck covered in leaves
funFacts: Wetting enhances a raccoon's sense of touch, which is why they seem to 'wash' their food.
Raccoons can remember the solution to a puzzle for up to three years.
Raccoons can solve Sudoku.

name: Blue-ringed Octopus
altText: A blue-ringed octopus displaying its iridescent blue rings
funFacts: Its venom can kill a person within minutes, and there is no antivenom.
Its blue rings flash brighter as a warning display right before it bites.
The blue-ringed octopus has the right of way on the high seas.

name: Pufferfish
altText: A baby pufferfish
funFacts: Pufferfish contain tetrodotoxin, a poison deadlier than cyanide with no known antidote.
Pufferfish inflate by rapidly gulping water into a highly elastic stomach.
Pufferfish cannot un-puff once they have puffed.
